title: Deepika and Ranveer Seek Siddhivinayak Blessings Ahead of Second Child's Birth
excerpt: The couple repeated the Siddhivinayak pilgrimage they made before daughter Dua's birth, arriving in matching purple as Ganeshotsav filled Mumbai.
body:
• Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone visited Mumbai's Siddhivinayak Temple on Friday to seek blessings ahead of the birth of their second child.
  • The couple arrived hand-in-hand in coordinated purple traditional wear — Deepika in an embellished ethnic ensemble, Ranveer in a purple kurta with white trousers — with Deepika's baby bump prominently visible.
  • The visit repeats a family tradition: they sought blessings at the same temple before the birth of their daughter Dua in September 2024.
  • A day earlier, Ranveer visited the Lalbaugcha Raja pandal during Ganeshotsav, where he pledged to support the education of 1,000 girls.

Bollywood's star couple turned a temple visit into a family ritual this week. Ranveer Singh and Deepika Padukone arrived at Mumbai's Siddhivinayak Temple on Friday to seek the blessings of Lord Ganesha ahead of the arrival of their second child, repeating the visit they made before their daughter Dua was born in September 2024.

The couple walked in hand-in-hand in colour-coordinated traditional wear. Deepika, visibly pregnant and careful with her baby bump, wore an intricately embellished ethnic ensemble in shades of purple and earthy tones; Ranveer complemented her in a rich purple kurta with white trousers. Photographs showed Ranveer protectively holding Deepika's hand as they entered and later guiding her back to their car.

Faith before the second arrival

The timing carries meaning for the couple. Dua turned two this month, and the pair recently released a series of intimate black-and-white maternity photographs on the occasion of her birthday — a rare public glimpse into a family life they have otherwise kept private, shielding their daughter from the spotlight.

The Siddhivinayak visit continues a pattern: before Dua's birth, the couple made the same pilgrimage. For a pair that guards its privacy, the public temple appearances before each birth have become the family's way of marking the milestone.

Ganeshotsav week

The visit came during Ganeshotsav 2026, and Ranveer's temple circuit began a day earlier. On Thursday he visited the Lalbaugcha Raja — the famed Navsacha Ganapati in Mumbai's Currey Road area, among the country's most visited Ganapati mandals — dressed in a white kurta-pyjama and accompanied by heavy security.

Speaking to Network18 after his darshan, Ranveer said he had come to thank Bappa for a successful year. "The past year has been filled with happiness for me and my family, thanks to Bappa's blessings. I came here, had his darshan, and thanked him," he said, adding he had sought blessings "for the journey ahead." He also pledged to join the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan and support the education of 1,000 girls, saying he hoped it would please Bappa.

"I sought his blessings for the journey ahead."

— Ranveer Singh, after visiting Lalbaugcha Raja

What's next for the couple

On the work front, Ranveer has begun shooting for Pralay, while Deepika will next be seen alongside Shah Rukh Khan in King — a project she is expected to return to after the delivery. For now, the couple's calendar is measured in weeks, not releases, and Mumbai's most photographed parents are about to become parents of two.

nri_angle: Deepika and Ranveer's temple pilgrimage before each child's birth resonates with diaspora families who keep their own faith traditions alive across continents.
